title: Studio Apartment Ideas: Layouts, Dividers & Decor
h1: Studio Apartment Ideas: Layouts for Every Size, Smart Dividers and Decor That Feels Expensive
description: Studio apartment ideas that work: layouts for 400, 500 and 600 sq ft studios, how to divide a studio apartment, furniture sizes, and decorating tips.
secondary_keywords: how to divide a studio apartment
excerpt: Layouts for 400, 500 and 600 sq ft studios, smart room dividers, and decorating choices that make one room work as four.
image_alt: Studio apartment ideas shown in an open-plan studio with a bookcase divider separating the bed from a cozy living area
key_takeaways: Place the bed first, as far from the front door as practical, so the entry view is the living zone.
Keep a clear 30 to 36 inch path from the door to the kitchen, bathroom, and bed.
Use open or movable dividers, such as open-back bookcases or curtains, so you do not block daylight.
Choose a 72 to 84 inch sofa, a storage bed, and a 36 inch round table for most studios.
Repeat one palette in every zone and give each zone its own light source.

faq.q: How do you divide a studio apartment?
faq.a: Use open or movable dividers that keep daylight flowing: an open-back bookcase between 48 and 72 inches tall, a floor-to-ceiling curtain on a track or tension rod, a folding screen, or a sofa floated with its back to the bed. Rugs and separate light sources for each zone add invisible borders without any construction.

faq.q: Where should the bed go in a studio apartment?
faq.a: Put the bed as far from the front door as practical, ideally along the far wall near but not blocking a window. That way the first thing you see on entering is the living area. If the bed must be visible from the door, screen it with a bookcase, a curtain, or a tall headboard.

faq.q: Can you fit a queen bed in a 400 sq ft studio?
faq.a: Yes, a queen bed (60 x 80 inches) can fit in many 400 square foot studios, but it leaves less room for seating and dining. A full bed or a Murphy bed often works better at that size. Draw the plan to scale first and make sure you still have a 30 inch walkway beside the bed.

faq.q: How do I make my studio apartment look bigger?
faq.a: Choose furniture on visible legs, keep one consistent color palette throughout, hang curtains high and wide, and place a large mirror where it reflects window light. Use closed storage to hide clutter, size your rug generously, and light each zone separately so corners do not disappear after dark.

faq.q: What size sofa is best for a studio apartment?
faq.a: Most studios suit a sofa 72 to 84 inches wide and no more than 36 inches deep. In studios under 450 square feet, a 72 inch sofa or loveseat with slim arms is usually the best fit. Avoid large sectionals unless the studio is closer to 600 square feet.
